doc.title: Hank Cicalo interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 30, 2022

title: Favorite rhythm sections: New York and L.A. A bands
summary: Hank praises the New York players, Richard Tee, Steve Gadd, Ralph McDonald, Hugh McCracken and Eric Gale, and the on-call A band system.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who did you like to see especially coming on a date as far as the rhythm section players? Did you have favorite drummers?

Oh, oh yea. You have favorite drummers, you have favorite bass players. And strangely — well not strangely enough — I mean the guys that work together, for example like in New York I always — the New York players, I loved the way New York players play, what Steve Gadd played with Richard Tee, and always those New York guys had a different feel. Because they worked together so often and they knew how each — you know. In L.A. it was different because you’d have — like in New York what I’m talking about was it was an A band. The A band was Richard Tee, I’m trying — but they had a rhythm section that was their rhythm section and it worked for almost everybody. They wanted the best guys.
It was always Ralph McDonald on percussion and you know the same guitar players.
But in L.A. that was different then.

Well the New York, since in New York there was a clique of guys, maybe ten guys. They worked all the time. Be it two bass players or two drummers or whatever. In other words they were like the on-call guys. They worked all the time. And then there were a lot of other guys that worked. Like at that point it was up to the producer or arranger wanting a special member or something. But there was always an A band, I’ll put it that way. The A bands in New York for a long time was Richard Tee, Steve Gadd on drums, Ralph McDonald percussion, I mean Hugh McCracken on guitar, Eric Gale on guitar. Those were the A guys. Same thing here in L.A.
